### Position read
Opening position. Red has advanced from (0,3) to the center at (3,3); all loss counts remain zero. The opponent will likely contest the center immediately.

### Our plan
Develop Red and Yellow toward complementary central squares while keeping clear rook lanes. Contest opposing central pieces with same-color sandwich setups; avoid accidentally capturing our teammate in mixed lines. Track instant center wins after every move.

### Opponent tendencies
No moves observed yet.

### Lessons
A piece may safely move into a sandwich. Only the moving color can form capture flanks, and captures are checked solely around its landing square.

### Position read
We occupy (3,3) with Red and (4,3) with Yellow; the opponent occupies (3,4) with Blue. All losses are zero. The remaining center square is (4,4). Yellow on (4,3) is presently safe from an immediate same-color sandwich.

### Our plan
Red threatens to capture Blue at (3,4) by moving from (0,5) to (3,5), using Red at (3,3) as the far flank. Expect Green to block column 5; if it does, exploit the displaced Green and preserve our two-square center column. Track enclosure and friendly-fire risks around the compact center.

### Opponent tendencies
Blue immediately contested Red’s first central occupation by taking the adjacent center square.

### Lessons
Avoid placing Yellow at (4,4): Blue could later land at (5,4) and sandwich it against Blue at (3,4). Same-team colors do not provide sandwich flanks.

### Position read
We occupy center squares (3,3) with Red and (4,3) with Yellow. Red has moved to (3,5), sandwiching and capturing Blue from (3,4), so Blue now has 1 loss. Green recently moved from (4,0) to (4,2), adjacent to our Yellow at (4,3). Our losses remain zero.

### Our plan
Defend the center pair and seek safe occupation of (3,4) and (4,4). Yellow may be able to exploit Green at (4,2), but only a Yellow far flank can enable a sandwich. Watch for the opponent using Green’s new position to pressure Yellow or obstruct central movement. Red at (3,5) and (3,3) create useful same-color flanks across row 3.

### Opponent tendencies
Blue contested the center immediately. Green responded by moving beside our Yellow rather than blocking Red’s announced column-5 capture.

### Lessons
Same-color flanks create the captures; teammate pieces do not. Before filling a center square, check whether an opponent can land beyond it and sandwich it against an existing piece of that opponent’s color.

### Position read
We hold (3,3) with Red and (4,3) with Yellow. Yellow moved from (7,5) to (4,5), sandwiching Blue at (4,4) against Yellow at (4,3); Blue now has 2 losses. Red also holds (3,5), while Green is at (4,2).

### Our plan
Complete center occupation: on Red’s next turn, move Red from (3,5) to (3,4) if still legal. Then Yellow can move from (4,5) to (4,4) for an immediate center victory. Check each intervening opponent move for captures or newly occupied center squares, but neither opponent currently has a direct route to (3,4) or (4,4).

### Opponent tendencies
Blue repeatedly contests the center, creating sandwich opportunities. Green has approached our Yellow from the left but lacks a same-color piece on the far side to capture it.

### Lessons
A center invader can become tactically vulnerable when our same-colored pieces can flank it. Always test direct center wins before pursuing elimination.

### Position read
We occupy three center squares: Red at (3,3) and (3,4), Yellow at (4,3). The last center square, (4,4), is empty. Yellow at (4,5) can enter it in one step. Blue has 2 losses; no color is eliminated.

### Our plan
If (4,4) remains empty and Yellow at (4,5) survives, move Yellow from (4,5) to (4,4) for immediate center victory. Before moving, verify that Green’s intervening turn did not capture a center holder or occupy (4,4). If the direct win is disrupted, prioritize restoring four-center control.

### Opponent tendencies
Blue contests the center and has already suffered two losses there. Green is approaching from the left, currently at (3,2) and (4,2), so it may try to disrupt our central formation.

### Lessons
Check the immediate center-win sequence first. Same-color sandwich requirements mean adjacent opponent pressure alone is not necessarily a capture threat.

### Position read
We occupy all four central squares after Yellow moves from (4,5) to (4,4): Red holds (3,3) and (3,4), while Yellow holds (4,3) and (4,4).

### Our plan
The move completes center occupation and wins immediately.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent contested the center but could not disrupt the prepared winning formation.

### Lessons
Always check for an immediate center-occupation win before considering captures or defensive moves.
